sources.entry: akou - Open-source call and meeting recorder that transcribes on-device with speaker labels and lets Claude Code or Codex question a call over MCP. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/GeiserX/akou) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: akou
summary.one_liner: akou is an open-source macOS desktop app that records calls on your own computer, transcribes them on-device with speaker labels, and lets your terminal agent (Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client) question a call while it runs.
use_cases: Record a call on a Mac without a bot joining the meeting
Get a live transcript with speaker labels during a call
Ask an AI agent questions about a call while it is in progress
Export finished call transcripts as Markdown to a notes vault or wiki
Dictate text into any app on macOS
Run a self-hosted transcription server in Docker
summary.what_it_does: Records the microphone and call audio on separate channels, using the whole computer or a single app as the audio source, with no virtual audio driver. It shows a live transcript while people speak and runs a final accurate pass with speaker labels on the Mac, with a timestamp on every line. A timestamped notepad lets you mark bullets, action items, questions and sections during the call. Ask answers questions about the call using a small locally built context via Claude Code, Codex, a local model, or your own API key, and falls back to "Search this call" with no provider. Every window action is also exposed through a local API, CLI and MCP so agents can start, follow and annotate calls.
notable: No bot in the meeting, no account, no cloud; audio and transcripts stay on disk
Agents (Claude Code, Codex, MCP) can question a call while it runs via local API/CLI
Separate microphone and call-audio channels without a virtual audio driver
Docker server image offers OpenAI-compatible, Wyoming and Bazarr endpoints
caveats: Desktop app runs on macOS only, Apple silicon with macOS 14.4 or later; the CLI on Linux and Windows cannot record
Speech models are a one-time download of about 3.0 GB
